owner_approval: Olesia (human-in-the-loop, required before any download/implementation step)
purpose: Machine-readable checklist for Hermes to (1) detect missing skills/knowledge, (2) search GitHub for candidate open-source solutions, (3) run a mandatory safety scan before touching any code, (4) only then download and implement, with human approval gates.

safety_tool.name: Microsoft Application Inspector
safety_tool.what_it_does: Static source-code analyzer that scans an open-source repo BEFORE you use it and reports what the code actually does: crypto usage, network calls, shell/OS operations, cloud API calls, and other risk signals. Designed specifically to vet third-party open-source components before adoption.
safety_tool.decision_rule: If Application Inspector flags unexplained network calls, shell execution, or obfuscated code in a repo you did not expect that from, STOP and do not run it. Ask a human (Olesia) before proceeding.

related_tools_optional.name: GitHub CodeQL
related_tools_optional.note: GitHub's (Microsoft-owned) static analysis engine; more focused on finding vulnerabilities than characterizing behavior. Good second layer for actively maintained repos with GitHub Actions enabled.

related_tools_optional.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud - agentless code scanning
related_tools_optional.note: Enterprise-tier scanning for repos/pipelines; likely overkill for a solo builder, mentioned for completeness only.

acquisition_pipeline.name: Detect gap
acquisition_pipeline.action: Hermes compares current project requirements against Olesia's known skill/tool inventory (see skill_gap_assessment below) and flags anything marked 'missing' or 'partial' that blocks the current task.

acquisition_pipeline.name: Search GitHub
acquisition_pipeline.action: Hermes searches GitHub for a repo/library that fills the specific gap (not a generic keyword search — must match the exact blocking need).

acquisition_pipeline.name: Shortlist
acquisition_pipeline.action: Hermes proposes 1-3 candidate repos with: stars, last commit date, license, and 1-line description. Presents to Olesia before downloading anything.

acquisition_pipeline.name: MANDATORY safety scan
acquisition_pipeline.action: Before any code from the shortlisted repo is downloaded to Olesia's MacBook, run Microsoft Application Inspector against the repo (can be run against the GitHub URL after a shallow clone to a throwaway temp folder).

acquisition_pipeline.name: Human review of scan
acquisition_pipeline.action: Hermes summarizes Application Inspector's findings in plain language. Olesia approves or rejects before proceeding.

acquisition_pipeline.name: Download
acquisition_pipeline.action: Only after approval: clone/download the repo into the correct project folder.

acquisition_pipeline.name: Implement
acquisition_pipeline.action: Integrate the code, run it in an isolated/test branch first, never directly on production or the main branch.

acquisition_pipeline.name: Log
acquisition_pipeline.action: Hermes logs the acquired skill/tool in Obsidian (Daily Log) and updates the skill_gap_assessment status from 'missing' to 'have'.

kanban_separation.principle: Learning tasks must never mix with LexFlow CRM build tasks on the same board, so daily CRM progress tracking stays clean.
kanban_separation.instruction_to_hermes: Create a NEW, separate project/board in the CRM tool called 'Learning & Skill Acquisition'. Do not add its cards to the existing LexFlow CRM build Kanban. Cross-link only by adding a reference tag (e.g. 'blocks: CRM-upgrade') on relevant cards so the two boards stay linked without merging.
kanban_separation.review_cadence: Weekly, during the 'Final review: checkpoint' session already in the Learning Plan sheet.
